# Implementing a Lock-Free Work-Stealing Scheduler in Swift: Part 2 – Core Data Structures and Atomic Operations

In the previous part of this tutorial, we laid the groundwork for understanding what a work-stealing scheduler is and why it's beneficial for concurrent task execution. We also began discussing the design principles behind lock-free programming and introduced the basic structure of our scheduler. Now, we'll dive deep into the implementation details, focusing on the core data structures and atomic operations that make our scheduler both efficient and safe.
